target_customer: Tech companies paying recruiting fees to hire engineers, plus engineers as free candidates
problem: Engineering hiring relied on resumes and repeated interviews, so strong candidates without credentials were missed.
business_model: Recruiting marketplace charging a percentage of first year salary, then subscription

founders.name: Ammon Bartram
founders.background_notes: Prior startup per FlexJobs listing; YC page lists him as Founder/CEO.

exit.reason: Karat bought the assessment product and team; the sourcing business and talent network were shut down March 31, 2023.

technical_complexity.rationale: Quiz platform, scheduling and matching; the hard part was operations and assessment design, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Assessment data on candidates helped but recruiting was a services business with low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HackerRank and Karat served the screening job; Karat bought the assessment tech in 2023.

market_need_then: Engineers were scarce and hiring slow; TechCrunch in 2015 said it was already profitable and placing people monthly, and in 2018 reported a 40 percent placement rate versus 20 percent industry standard.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known to engineers and the YC network and used by Apple and Dropbox, but no source shows the brand as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Triplebyte raised about 48 million dollars by 2019 and placed engineers at top companies, then sold its assessment product to Karat in March 2023 and closed its sourcing business. Sources do not state why, so no failure factor is assigned beyond noting the 2022 to 2023 hiring slowdown as context.
notes: triplebyte.com returned 503. Series B date conflicts (April 1 vs April 11, 2019). The 2018 TechCrunch mentions an earlier 4.5M seed versus 3M in 2015, unreconciled, hence partial coverage. No dated competitor sources opened (TechCrunch 2015 did not name competitors); HackerRank and Hired appear only in later alternatives lists. Founder education not found. Pivot detail not researched.
